title: B1 · Thorough
content: Thorough — detailed and careful; done completely.
translation: Exhaustivo / minucioso. Ejemplo: She did a thorough review of the essay.

title: B1 · Reliable
content: Reliable — someone or something you can trust or depend on.
translation: Confiable. Ejemplo: He's a reliable classmate; he always delivers on time.

title: B2 · Straightforward
content: Straightforward — clear, simple, and easy to understand.
translation: Claro / directo. Ejemplo: The instructions were straightforward.

title: B1 · Deadline
content: Deadline — the latest time or date by which something must be finished.
translation: Fecha límite. Ejemplo: The deadline for the assignment is Friday.

title: B2 · Overwhelm
content: Overwhelm — to make someone feel too much pressure or emotion.
translation: Abrumar. Ejemplo: Don't let the exam overwhelm you; study step by step.

title: B1 · Feedback
content: Feedback — comments or advice about how well you did something.
translation: Retroalimentación / comentarios. Ejemplo: Ask your teacher for feedback on your speaking.

title: B1 · Look forward to
content: Look forward to + -ing/noun — to feel excited about something that will happen.
translation: Esperar con ganas. Ejemplo: I look forward to meeting you next week.

title: B1 · Give up
content: Give up — to stop trying; to quit.
translation: Rendirse / dejar. Ejemplo: Don't give up if the listening feels hard at first.

title: B2 · Catch up on
content: Catch up on — to do something you haven't had time to do; to get the latest news.
translation: Ponerse al día. Ejemplo: I need to catch up on my homework this weekend.

title: B1 · Figure out
content: Figure out — to understand or solve something after thinking about it.
translation: Entender / resolver. Ejemplo: I can't figure out this grammar rule.

title: B2 · Bring up
content: Bring up — to start talking about a topic.
translation: Mencionar / sacar un tema. Ejemplo: She brought up an interesting point in the forum.

title: B1 · Run out of
content: Run out of — to have no more of something left.
translation: Quedarse sin. Ejemplo: We ran out of time during the exam.

title: B1 · Listening · Daily routine
content: I usually wake up at seven, have breakfast, and then study English for twenty minutes.
translation: Normalmente me despierto a las siete, desayuno y después estudio inglés veinte minutos.

title: B1 · Listening · At the café
content: Could I have a large coffee with milk, please? And a piece of chocolate cake.
translation: ¿Me podría dar un café grande con leche, por favor? Y un trozo de torta de chocolate.

title: B2 · Listening · Giving an opinion
content: In my opinion, practicing a little every day is more effective than studying for hours once a week.
translation: En mi opinión, practicar un poco todos los días es más efectivo que estudiar horas una vez por semana.

title: B2 · Listening · Making plans
content: Are you free on Saturday afternoon? I was thinking we could review the phrasal verbs together.
translation: ¿Estás libre el sábado a la tarde? Pensaba que podríamos repasar los phrasal verbs juntos.

title: B2 · Worthwhile
content: Worthwhile — useful, valuable, or worth the time and effort.
translation: Que vale la pena. Ejemplo: Watching short English videos is a worthwhile habit.

title: B2 · Come across
content: Come across — to find something by chance; to seem a certain way.
translation: Encontrar por casualidad / dar la impresión. Ejemplo: I came across a great podcast yesterday.
